svg.text: THE FACADE — where the saga lives
the ONLY place cross-service orchestration happens ✓
putting it in CartService would make the cart know about orders and stock
searchProducts is an O(n) scan with toLowerCase per product
soft delete keeps historic orders resolvable — costs status filtering everywhere
depends on ProductService to resolve product + price
a cart NEVER reserves stock — that is checkout's job
was: if (order != null) { ... } — a silent no-op that reported success
THE MODEL — the invariant lives IN the entity
Product — the class the whole problem is about
price: BigDecimal — never double, money is exact
rating: double · reviewCount: int ← must move TOGETHER
boolean tryReserve(int qty) — a CAS loop, the heart of the design
if (current < quantity) return false; // not enough
releaseStock(qty) · addStock(qty) · reduceStock(qty) — throws instead of false
synchronized updateRating(newRating) — rating AND reviewCount in one step
the loop is not a spin lock: it retries only when another thread SUCCEEDED, so the system always progresses
paymentId: String — a REFERENCE, not a Payment
guarded methods, NOT a State class hierarchy ✓
OrderItem: productId, name, price SNAPSHOT, qty
a later catalog price change must not rewrite
cost: duplicated data you cannot correct
retroactively — which is usually what you want
Review (rating + comment) → feeds Product.updateRating · review list is a CopyOnWriteArrayList (read-often, write-rare)
Customer · Address (VO) · Payment / PaymentMethod / PaymentStatus · Category / ProductCategory
a plain ArrayList inside a ConcurrentHashMap loses concurrent adds — a mistake that LOOKS safe
ORDER LIFECYCLE — legality in the entity
cancel() RELEASES each line's quantity back to the catalog ✓
without that symmetry, inventory leaks on every cancellation
THE ONE INVARIANT: don't sell what you don't have
The original checkout never consulted or decremented stock at all.
stock at start = 1 · orders placed = 100 · stock now = 1
An empty cart also produced a valid order with 0 items and a total of 0,
while EmptyCartException sat in the codebase entirely unreferenced.
WHY tryReserve LIVES ON Product, NOT ProductService
A service method can be bypassed by the next person who writes a
new service. An entity that refuses to go negative cannot be.
Every buyer passes the check against the same stale read.
compare + decrement must be ONE step — that is compareAndSet ✓
① Amazon facade (checkout is the saga) → ② the four service seams → ③ Product.tryReserve — the CAS that IS the design → ④ Order's guarded transitions → ⑤ the oversell reproduction

g.text: Patterns: Facade · Service Layer + DI · Value Object (price snapshot) · lightweight State (guarded methods) · CAS · Saga with compensation
Observer (order notifications) and Strategy (pricing / discounts) are named but NOT built — no client requires them yet
In a database this CAS becomes UPDATE product SET stock = stock − ? WHERE id = ? AND stock >= ?, checked by affected-row count
